an isolated checkout.

🔴 THIS IS LEG 2 OF A THREE-FLIGHT STAGED SPLIT. READ THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE.

The plan for this brief requires THREE STRICTLY SEQUENTIAL legs with blocking
hand-offs (L1 design -> L2 classify -> L3 route). The fleet harness cuts all legs
in PARALLEL from one base — verified in `workflows/fleet-dev/fleet_dev.awl`
(`step open` / `distribute leg in legs`; `concurrency 3` is "the parallel-legs
value — one lane per leg"). So the split runs as three flights, one leg each,
each based on the previous flight's result head. You are standing on L1's.

**L1 IS DONE AND ITS ARTIFACT IS ON THIS TREE:**
`docs/design/policy-refused-fallback.md`. It is AUTHORITATIVE for every design
decision in this leg. It decided, among other things: `PolicyRefused` is
stochastic with `is_deterministic() == false`; detection is ADAPTER-LOCAL for
both norn and ACP; `ActivityErrorKind::PolicyRefused` is the F-1 wire choice;
hop-first with configured no-chain retries and no minted bound.

**THIS FLIGHT IS L2 ONLY.** Do NOT implement the AWL `fallback` declaration,
engine chain consultation, replay determinism, or `resolve_task_queue`. Those are
L3 and they fly on top of your head. A leg that reaches into L3 breaks the
ordering the whole plan rests on.

⚠️ TWO KNOWN DEFECTS IN THE L1 RECORD, from its judge — read around them:
- `.fleet/reports/l1-design.md`'s citations INTO ITS OWN ARTIFACT are uniformly
  two lines early (e.g. `:132-143` for content at `:134-145`) — and the artifact
  has since gained a section, moving anchors further. Trust the ARTIFACT and
  re-derive any anchor from it by heading; never navigate by the report's line
  numbers.
- The report's validation lists no `git ls-tree` receipt; the judge ran it
  itself and the tree was clean, so the fact holds — noted so you do not
  re-litigate it.

🔴 ONE PREMISE THE ARTIFACT NOW STATES EXPLICITLY, AND IT BINDS YOUR CODE.
The design derives each fallback hop from the recorded initial queue, the prior
`ActivityFallbackRouted` events, and **the immutable authored fallback list**.
That list is immutable for a run because content-hash module namespacing binds a
running workflow to the package version it started with; `ContinuedAsNew` starts
a new run and re-derives.

⇒ Wherever you touch the authored list, read it from the run's OWN bound module
version — NEVER from whatever is currently deployed. The current-deploy reading
is the natural one, it looks identical in every test, and it breaks replay only
for a workflow that was mid-hop when a new version landed. That is precisely the
long-lived-workflow failure this engine exists not to have, and it is invisible
until it matters.

⛔ **IMPLEMENT THE ARTIFACT'S DECISIONS AND ONLY THOSE.** Where your leg brief
and the artifact disagree, THE ARTIFACT WINS — it was written with this tree in
hand. If the artifact left something genuinely OPEN, that is a defect in L1:
REPORT IT AND STOP on that point rather than deciding it here. Deciding an open
design question inside an implementation leg is how a design-first split quietly
becomes a design-last one.

Read, in this order and in this order of authority:
1. `.fleet/BRIEF.md` §CORRECTION (:3-27) — binding, outranks the body.
2. `docs/evidence/policy-refused-census-20260822.md` — the measurement.
3. `.fleet/plan.md` — especially §0 (missed sites), §1 (re-derived seams),
   §2 (the load-bearing fact), §3 (findings F-1, F-2, F-3).
4. `.fleet/legs/l2-classify.md` — YOUR leg brief, authoritative for your
   SCOPE. But `docs/design/policy-refused-fallback.md` is authoritative for
   every DECISION, and where they disagree the artifact wins.
5. `.fleet/BRIEF.md` body — subject to §0.

🔴 THE BINDING CORRECTION — read `.fleet/BRIEF.md` from the top; its §CORRECTION
(:3-27) OUTRANKS the body wherever they disagree, and the measurement behind it
is committed at `docs/evidence/policy-refused-census-20260822.md`.

In one line: a provider policy refusal is STOCHASTIC, not deterministic for its
content. Workflow 4ddee56c refused act 1 on attempt 1 and COMPLETED act 1 on
attempt 2 — same act, same content. aion#65 round 3 shows it independently.

🔴 THE TWO REFUTED SITES HAVE SINCE BEEN SWEPT — READ THE RECONCILIATION.
The flight1 counsel found (b) and (d) still stating the refuted premise inline
in the body and named them in `.fleet/plan.md` §0 as MISSED SITE 1
(`.fleet/BRIEF.md:86-87`) and MISSED SITE 2 (`:116-118`). That finding was
correct and has been ACTED ON: both now read correctly in the body.

⇒ `.fleet/BRIEF.md` opens with a RECONCILIATION block. Read it. The "unswept"
claim is repeated across FIVE documents — `.fleet/plan.md` §0 and its M1/M2
index rows, and all three leg briefs — and every one of them is historical ON
THAT POINT ONLY. They were deliberately left byte-identical because they are the
counsel's record and the evidence for the correction. Wherever one says a site
is "refuted AND UNSWEPT", read "refuted, and SINCE CORRECTED in the body". Every
RULING they draw is unchanged and still binding.

⇒ Do NOT go to those line numbers expecting refuted text. A line number still
resolves after the text moves and resolves to the wrong thing.

⇒ Several documents still cite the pre-sweep line numbers. Anywhere one asks you
to supersede `.fleet/BRIEF.md:86-87` or `:116-118`, discharge it against the
PROPOSITIONS, not the coordinates: the original (b) ("deterministic — will refuse
this content every time") and the original (d) ("fail FAST … no in-place
retries"). L1's artifact already recorded that supersession; you implement it,
you do not re-argue it.

DELIVER — implementation of the artifact's decisions, and only those:

R2(a) THE CLASS. `HarnessError::PolicyRefused` exists in `aion-integrations`,
with its `is_deterministic()` arm decided as the artifact decided it (the
artifact's answer is `false` — a refusal is stochastic; implement THAT, and do
not re-argue it). The enum is `#[non_exhaustive]` and its match is exhaustive by
doctrine, so sweep every site the plan lists — including the CATCH-ALLS that
would swallow the new variant silently, and the doc that would go stale.

R2(b) DETECTION, ADAPTER-LOCAL, BOTH ADAPTERS. Per the artifact: detection lives
INSIDE the adapter, not in the `AdvisingHarness` decorator — the decorator sits
above the seam where the structured carrier is already dropped, so classifying
there would force exactly the substring matching this design rejects.
- norn: the structured refusal must be caught before `response_into_payload`
  flattens it to prose. 🔴 MEASURED FACT, do not design against it: the provider's
  `code` (e.g. `cyber_policy`) DOES NOT SURVIVE into the string norn hands out —
  evidence in `gate-logs/dev-worker-0150.log:589` (raw frame) vs `:590` (what is
  handed out). So the spelling is NOT available at aion's altitude and detection
  must key on STRUCTURE, never on that substring.
- ACP: it already expresses a typed refusal — `StopReason::Refusal`
  (`translate.rs:291`), discriminated at `outcome.rs:152-154` but folded in with
  `MaxTokens`/`MaxTurnRequests`. Unfold it.

R2(c) THE WIRE + THE GRAMMAR. Implement the artifact's F-1 choice
(`ActivityErrorKind::PolicyRefused`). Any generated types are REGENERATED, never
hand-edited. The Gleam grammar gains its arm so a policy refusal presents as
ITSELF and never as "activity engine failure" through the fallthrough.

R3(1) and R3(4) GREEN, both directions tested: a synthetic structured policy
refusal classifies as `PolicyRefused`, AND an ordinary harness error still
classifies as retryable `Harness`. A test that only proves the new path is half a
test — the regression it invites is everything becoming `PolicyRefused`.

🔴 NEVER write a test asserting the no-chain path fails after exactly ONE
attempt, whatever any text says. That pins, as a passing assertion, the behaviour
that would have killed workflow 4ddee56c. Assert the CLASSIFICATION and that no
chain hop was attempted; assert NO particular attempt count. The invariant, not
the enumeration. Do not MINT a retry bound as a literal — it is configured.

SCOPE WALL: no AWL `fallback` word, no engine chain consultation, no replay
determinism work, no `resolve_task_queue`. That is L3 and it flies on your head.

PROCESS WALLS — binding, from the brief and the house rules:
- No lint suppressions in any spelling. No #[ignore] in any spelling — a test
  needing a runtime gates it AT RUNTIME (read an env var, emit a tracing::info!
  skip line, return Ok(())).
- No file over 500 lines. thiserror for library errors; never .unwrap() or
  .expect() in library code; lock poison mapped to a typed error.
- Wire/TS changes, if the design chooses them, are REGENERATED — never
  hand-edited generated types.
- ⛔ Never one blocking sleep sized to the expected duration. Poll, with a total
  deadline, and timeout as its own distinct outcome.
- Do NOT widen scope to the pre-existing `exhausted:`/`infrastructure:`
  fallthrough mislabelling. It is F-3 in the plan, REPORT ONLY.
- MEASURED RED IS A SUCCESS OUTCOME. If the design pass concludes the fallback
  hop cannot be made replay-deterministic without restructuring beyond this
  scope, that conclusion WITH EVIDENCE is the deliverable — committed and
  reported. No heroics, no silent narrowing.

GROUNDING — `.fleet/plan.md` §1 re-derived every seam on THIS tree and flagged
what MOVED. Trust the plan's coordinates over the brief's, and re-check any you
rely on. Anchor on the SYMBOL name, never the line number: a positional
reference fails silently, because a line number still resolves after the code

IF YOUR OWN WORK TRIPS A POLICY REFUSAL: report it as a FIRST-CLASS FINDING with
what tripped and where. It is evidence for this very brief, not an obstacle to
route around. Do not rewrite the work to dodge the trigger. (The previous
planning pass recorded F-4: no policy refusal tripped it.)

KNOWN FLAKE, do not chase and do not suppress: aion#54, the shard-actor timeout,
measured at 2 of 24 on base and 2 of 24 on branch — it is ambient and unrelated
to this work. If it appears in a gate red, attribute it and move on.

WHEN DONE: write `.fleet/reports/l2-classify.md` — that exact lowercase path — and
COMMIT IT. 🔴 An uncommitted report is destroyed by the merge: fan-in merges
BRANCHES, so anything left in your working tree that is not committed does not
exist. Give a `git ls-tree` receipt for every file you claim to have written
before you declare done. Report only what you OBSERVED, with file:line, and

337	express a policy refusal."* **It can, and far more cleanly than norn.**

358	## 3. FINDINGS THAT ARE NOT IN THE BRIEF

361	findings, not scope.

364	
365	`crates/aion-server/src/worker/bridge.rs:475-490`:
366	
367	```rust
368	ActivityCompletionOutcome::Failed(error) => {
369	    let prefix = if error.is_retryable() { "retryable" } else { "terminal" };
370	    …
371	    Err(format!("{prefix}:{}", error.message))
372	}
373	```
374	
375	Every worker-originated reason string is minted **here**, from
376	`ActivityErrorKind`'s two variants and nothing else. There is no third prefix a
377	worker can produce. `timeout:`, `parked:`, `lost:`, `superseded:`,
378	`transport-exhausted:` and `exhausted:` are all synthesised ENGINE-side, never by
379	a worker.

389	### F-2 (ENABLING) — a structured detail channel already exists end-to-end and is unused
390	
391	- `ActivityFailure::with_detail(Payload)` — `crates/aion-worker/src/activity.rs:52-57`.
392	- Survives into `ActivityError.details` — `activity.rs:99-107` (`:104`).
393	- Crosses the worker protocol — `crates/aion-worker/src/protocol/session.rs:832`.
394	- Is **durably recorded**: `Event::ActivityFailed { error: ActivityError, attempt }`
395	  — `crates/aion-core/src/event.rs:469-478` — carries the whole `ActivityError`,
396	  `details` included.

398	  arms construct a bare `ActivityFailure::terminal/retryable(error.to_string())`.

401	history that costs no wire change and no TS regeneration, and today it carries
402	nothing on the agent path. It is a strong candidate for carrying the refusal
403	code (and the refusing queue) without touching `ActivityErrorKind`. **Caveat:**
404	`bridge.rs:490` reads only `error.message`, so `details` reaches history but does

1	# Policy-refused classification and declared provider fallback
2	
3	**Status:** L1 design decision, 2026-08-22
4	
5	**Scope:** design only; L2 implements classification and L3 implements routing
6	
7	**Evidence:** `docs/evidence/policy-refused-census-20260822.md`
8	
9	## Decision summary
10	
11	A provider policy refusal is a **stochastic routing fact**, not a deterministic
12	content fault. The system will:
13	
14	1. recognise the refusal inside each adapter before its typed discriminator is
15	   flattened;
16	2. expose it as `HarnessError::PolicyRefused` and
17	   `ActivityErrorKind::PolicyRefused`;
18	3. render it on the worker-to-engine reason wire as `policy_refused:`;
19	4. consult an authored queue fallback chain before considering any
20	   same-provider retry;
21	5. record every refusal and queue hop through the workflow's `Recorder`, so
22	   replay obtains the same queue sequence from history; and
23	6. retain a bounded same-provider retry when no chain is declared, using the
24	   act's configured retry policy rather than a bound invented here.
25	
26	This design supersedes two original propositions from `.fleet/BRIEF.md`:
27	
28	- It supersedes the original claim that the provider will refuse the same
29	  content every time. Workflow `4ddee56c` completed the same act on attempt 2
30	  after a `cyber_policy` refusal on attempt 1, and aion#65 round 3 independently
31	  survived the same pattern. There is no mechanism on this tree that turns
32	  those observed stochastic outcomes into deterministic ones.
33	- It supersedes the original instruction to fail fast with no in-place retry
34	  when no chain exists. That behavior would have killed both measured
35	  survivals. The no-chain path therefore retains the act's configured bounded
36	  retry behavior.
37	
38	The design does **not** address the existing unparsed engine-side prefixes
39	listed as finding F-3 in `.fleet/plan.md`; that remains report-only scope.
40	
41	## Evidence and constraints
42	
43	The census found four flights whose providers kept refusing across their whole
44	budgets and at least two independent cases in which the same content cleared on
45	a later execution. It supports both routing away from a refusing provider and
46	retaining a configured no-chain retry. It does not support any newly chosen
47	retry count.
48	
49	The tracked frame at `gate-logs/dev-worker-0150.log:589` contains the upstream
50	structured path `error.code = "cyber_policy"`. The next line, which is what norn
51	hands to aion, contains only the prose `"provider rejected the request under its
52	cybersecurity policy"`; the code has disappeared. The JSON-RPC application code
53	seen by aion is the generic `-32603`, so it cannot identify a refusal.
54	
55	A provider change cannot be an in-process model rotation. The measured norn
56	harness is ChatGPT-only, AWL has no model field, and task queue is the existing
57	pool/flavour selector (`PoolAddress` in
58	`crates/aion-server/src/worker/registry.rs`). A fallback is therefore a
59	queue/harness hop.
60	
61	## R1-a — recognition belongs inside the adapters
62	
63	### Norn
64	
65	**Primary site:**
66	`crates/aion-integration-norn/src/session.rs::response_into_payload`.
67	
68	This is the last attested aion-owned point holding
69	`JsonRpcError { code, message, data }`. Recognition happens before the existing
70	`HarnessError::harness(format!(...))` conversion. The one accepted structured
71	shape is the measured provider frame copied into JSON-RPC data:
72	`data.pointer("/error/code") == Some("cyber_policy")`. This exact path mirrors
73	`gate-logs/dev-worker-0150.log:589`; L2 must not recursively search arbitrary
74	JSON or accept look-alike keys. The tree does **not** attest that norn currently
75	populates this shape, so it is a narrowly specified capability rather than a
76	claim about today's norn output. The provider code value is evidence-attested,
77	not inferred from the generic JSON-RPC code.
78	
79	`JsonRpcError.code == -32603` is not a discriminator. The real-run fixture
80	`crates/aion-integration-norn/src/advice.rs::tests::RECORDED_REFUSAL` shows a
81	non-policy session refusal under that generic code, while the measured policy
82	refusal was also surfaced as an application-level run failure. The outer code
83	therefore identifies neither class. `error.data` is the only possible structured
84	JSON-RPC channel.
85	
86	When `error.data` is `None`, has an unknown shape, or does not carry the policy
87	code, norn cannot express this refusal structurally to aion today. The honest
88	fallback at this same adapter site is **textual** and deliberately narrow: match
89	the observed norn phrase
90	`provider rejected the request under its cybersecurity policy` in
91	`JsonRpcError.message`. The match is against that adapter-owned message field,
92	not against arbitrary transcript, prompt, output, or formatted
93	`HarnessError` text. The resulting refusal records that detection was textual
94	and preserves the original detail. Unmatched errors remain
95	`HarnessError::Harness`.
96	
97	**Secondary structured point:**
98	`crates/aion-integration-norn/src/translate/outcome.rs::outcome_into_payload`.
99	
100	The stop envelope remains structured until this function formats `stop` into
101	prose. On this tree the protocol names only `stop.reason = "completed"`; there
102	is no declared refusal value, and the measured refusal arrived through the
103	JSON-RPC error path. Therefore L2 must not guess that an arbitrary non-completion
104	stop is a policy refusal. This site recognises `PolicyRefused` only if the norn
105	wire contract gains an explicit refusal reason; otherwise its current
106	non-completions remain ordinary harness failures.
107	
108	`AdvisingHarness::advise` is not a detection site. It receives an already
109	flattened `HarnessError::Harness { detail: String }`, so putting recognition
110	there would make every path textual and would discard the available
111	`JsonRpcError.data` discriminator.
112	
113	### ACP
114	
115	**Site:** `crates/aion-integration-acp/src/outcome.rs::outcome_into_payload`, at
116	the branch over `prompt.stop_reason`, before
117	`outcome.rs::non_completion` flattens it.
118	
119	ACP recognition is **typed**:
120	`agent_client_protocol::StopReason::Refusal` maps directly to
121	`HarnessError::PolicyRefused`. `MaxTokens` and `MaxTurnRequests` do not. The
122	existing `non_completion` helper currently folds all three into one prose
123	`HarnessError::Harness`; L2 must split `Refusal` before that helper. The
124	JSON-RPC `prompt_error` function is not ACP's policy-refusal seam.
125	
126	## R1-b — class and stochastic classification
127	
128	`HarnessError` gains a harness-neutral `PolicyRefused` variant. It carries the
129	human-readable detail and may carry adapter-supplied structured diagnostic
130	metadata, such as the provider code and whether recognition was structured or
131	textual. Provider-specific names remain inside adapter construction; callers
132	route on the variant, never on prose.
133	
134	`HarnessError::is_deterministic()` returns **false** for `PolicyRefused`.
135	Exhibits A and B directly rule out `true`, and no contrary mechanism exists.
136	This answer describes the provider outcome's repeatability only; it does not
137	mean policy refusal should flow through the ordinary transient-retry branch.
138	
139	The binary `is_deterministic()` API cannot express “route first, retry second.”
140	Therefore `crates/aion-worker/src/runtime/agent.rs::harness_error_to_outcome`
141	must special-case `HarnessError::PolicyRefused` before its existing
142	`true -> terminal` / `false -> retryable` mapping. Ordinary errors continue to
143	use that binary. The new arm produces a dedicated policy-refused activity
144	failure, while `is_deterministic() == false` remains the truthful answer to the
145	narrow determinism question.
146	
147	L2 must also sweep the intervention catch-alls in
148	`agent.rs::deliver_dyn_command` and `agent.rs::apply_command`,
149	`crates/aion-integration-norn/src/advice.rs::advise`, and the classification
150	documentation above `harness_error_to_outcome`. A new variant must never be
151	silently collapsed by a wildcard.
152	
153	## R1-c — reason vocabulary and the F-1 choice
154	
155	This design chooses **F-1 option 1**: add
156	`ActivityErrorKind::PolicyRefused` in `crates/aion-core/src/error.rs`.
157	
158	The other choices are rejected:
159	
160	- Keeping `ActivityErrorKind` binary cannot produce a third worker-originated
161	  reason at `crates/aion-server/src/worker/bridge.rs`, which currently chooses
162	  only `retryable:` or `terminal:` from `error.is_retryable()`.
163	- Using only `ActivityError.details` would durably preserve metadata but would
164	  not reach the reason string parsed by the retry loop and Gleam grammar,
165	  because `bridge.rs` reads only `error.message`.
166	- Teaching the bridge to infer policy refusal from message/detail would move
167	  classification away from the adapter and recreate a second, drift-prone
168	  classifier.
169	
170	`ActivityFailure` therefore gains a dedicated constructor/classification that
171	converts to `ActivityErrorKind::PolicyRefused`. The worker/server bridge maps
172	that kind explicitly to `policy_refused:`. This is a wire change: update the
173	registered type in `crates/aion-core/src/generated_types.rs`, regenerate all
174	TypeScript bindings, and never hand-edit generated output.
175	
176	The reason string and details have separate duties:
177	
178	- `ActivityErrorKind::PolicyRefused` is the authoritative control signal.
179	  `bridge.rs` renders it as `policy_refused:`, the engine routes on that prefix,
180	  and Gleam parses it as its own public error class. It is neither ordinary
181	  `Retryable` nor final `Terminal`: `ActivityError::is_retryable()` stays false,
182	  while settlement/cursor code gains an explicit terminal predicate under which
183	  only `Terminal` settles an activity. A recorded `PolicyRefused` is therefore an
184	  intermediate routing/retry fact until the engine records a final disposition.
185	- `ActivityError.details` is **not** the end-to-end carrier for this flight.
186	  Although `ActivityFailure::with_detail` crosses the worker protocol, the
187	  server bridge returns only a prefixed `String` through
188	  `ActivityDispatcher::dispatch`, and the engine retry recorder reconstructs
189	  `ActivityError { details: None }`. Adapter metadata is therefore lost before
190	  engine history on this path. Routing correctness and the L2/L3 contract use
191	  only the dedicated kind/prefix. Preserving provider code and detection mode in
192	  durable engine history would require a structured dispatcher result instead
193	  of `Result<String, String>`; that restructuring is outside this flight.
194	
195	This resolves finding F-2 honestly: the available details channel and the
196	reason string are not reconciled by pretending they meet. The prefix is the
197	sole end-to-end **class** carrier; it does not encode finality. The retry loop's
198	own disposition carries finality, and the await seam records that disposition as
199	`ActivityErrorKind::Terminal` while preserving the `policy_refused:`-prefixed
200	message verbatim. The current detail loss is recorded as a limitation rather
201	than silently relied upon.
202	
203	## R1-d — declared fallback semantics
204	
205	AWL gains an ordered `fallback` list beside `retry` on `ActionConfig`. Entries
206	are task queues, not model names. The emitter and MIR lower the same authored
207	list into activity configuration. Duplicate entries are rejected during AWL
208	checking. At runtime, an entry equal to the current queue is skipped rather than
209	executed; the next distinct queue is the hop, and its original authored index is
210	what history records. This makes `fallback norn, claude` deterministic even when
211	the initial resolved queue is already `norn`, and it prevents a declared hop
212	from becoming a same-provider retry. This design adds no model field.
213	
214	For a policy-refused execution:
215	
216	1. Record the refusal as a nonterminal `ActivityFailed` with
217	   `ActivityErrorKind::PolicyRefused` and the execution attempt.
218	2. If an unconsumed distinct fallback queue exists, select it and record the hop
219	   before dispatching there.
220	3. Dispatch the same activity ordinal and input on that recorded queue.
221	4. If each distinct declared queue has refused, record/deliver the final
222	   disposition as `ActivityErrorKind::Terminal` whose reason begins
223	   `policy_refused:` and names the refusing queue sequence.
224	5. If no fallback chain was declared, apply the act's existing configured retry
225	   policy on the same queue. Each refusal with budget left remains a nonterminal
226	   `PolicyRefused` event. On exhaustion, record/deliver a final `Terminal` event
227	   whose reason begins `policy_refused:` with the attempts accounted; do not
228	   relabel it `exhausted:` or an engine fault.
229	
230	Thus **hop first, retry second**. A live chain consumes only its own ordered
231	entries. A policy refusal while the chain is live is not eligible in
232	`failure_stand_down`'s ordinary retryable branch and consumes no same-provider
233	retry budget.
234	
235	Execution identity and retry accounting must be separated. The existing
236	one-based `ActivityStarted.attempt` remains a monotonically increasing identity
237	for every actual execution, including a fallback execution. The authored retry
238	budget is no longer inferred solely from that global execution number: L3 must
239	track/derive same-provider retries separately, because a queue hop is an
240	execution but is not a same-provider retry. This preserves the `(workflow,
241	activity, attempt)` dedupe identity without charging a hop to `RetrySpec`.
242	
243	There is deliberately no numeric retry bound in this design. The no-chain path
244	uses the value resolved by `retry_policy_from_config` from the act's existing
245	`RetrySpec`; the census supplies no basis for another default.
246

247	## R1-e — history-derived replay
248	
249	A fallback hop is **not** a fourth input-precedence level in
250	`resolve_task_queue`. That function still chooses the initial queue exactly
251	once:
252	
253	1. per-activity override;
254	2. workflow-declared default;
255	3. start-time queue from recorded history; then
256	4. the existing named last resort.
257	
258	The resulting initial queue remains recorded in `Event::ActivityScheduled`.
259	Fallback is a post-failure override of that recorded initial choice.
260	
261	L3 adds a dedicated history event, named here
262	`Event::ActivityFallbackRouted`, with at least:
263	
264	- `activity_id`;
265	- the refusal execution attempt;
266	- `from_task_queue`;
267	- `to_task_queue`; and
268	- the zero-based position consumed from the authored fallback list.
269	
270	The hop is appended only through the workflow's existing `Recorder` held by
271	`RetryRecorderSeam`; no component calls `EventStore::append` directly. The
272	recorder guard re-reads the current run segment under the recorder lock before
273	adding the hop, so a settled ordinal, closed engine-task epoch, or already
274	recorded hop stands the detached completion task down.
275	
276	The order around a hop is durable:
277	
278	1. record the policy-refused `ActivityFailed` for the current queue;
279	2. derive the next list position from the recorded initial queue plus prior
280	   `ActivityFallbackRouted` events and the immutable authored list;
281	3. record `ActivityFallbackRouted` before the next dispatch;
282	4. record the next `ActivityStarted`; and
283	5. put the delivery on the recorded `to_task_queue`.
284	
285	A crash between (1) and (3) re-derives the same next queue and records it. A
286	crash after (3) reuses the event's `to_task_queue`; it does not consult live
287	worker availability or choose again. If recovery finds a trailing nonterminal
288	`PolicyRefused` and derives that no distinct hop or configured same-provider
289	retry remains, it must produce the same `RetryLoopTerminal::Failed` disposition
290	with a `policy_refused:` message; the normal await seam then records the final
291	`ActivityErrorKind::Terminal` event. Thus a crash after the last refusal but
292	before final delivery cannot leave the ordinal dangling or invent another
293	execution.
294	
295	Recovery and the replay cursor must treat `ActivityFallbackRouted` and
296	nonterminal `PolicyRefused` as part of the same activity span, just as they
297	already walk retryable `ActivityFailed` and later `ActivityStarted` events.
298	Queue selection and final exhaustion are therefore functions of history plus
299	the immutable activity configuration, never wall clock, fleet membership, or
300	provider availability.
301	
302	The terminal `policy_refused:` reason lists queues by the recorded sequence,
303	not by recomputing what might have happened. This makes the E2E claim auditable:
304	one refusal plus one hop, zero same-queue retries, and an empty final failure
305	reason when the fallback succeeds.
306	
307	This design is replay-deterministic within the existing architecture; measured
308	red is not required. It does require L3 to add the explicit event, recorder
309	method, cursor/recovery handling, and separate retry-budget accounting described
310	above. Omitting any one of those pieces would make the route implicit or charge
311	fallback executions against the wrong budget.
312	
313	### Why the authored list is immutable for a run
314	
315	*(Added post-gate by the flight owner: the derivation above relies on this
316	premise without stating it, which is the owner's finding on review, not a defect
317	in the gated design.)*
318	
319	The derivation above depends on the authored fallback list being **immutable for
320	the lifetime of a run**. It is, and the reason is worth stating because the
321	alternative reading is the natural one.
322	
323	Each `.aion` package version is a distinct, immutable module named by its content
324	hash (`logical_name$hash`). A running workflow is bound to the module version it
325	started with, so the fallback list it derives hops from cannot change underneath
326	it — a redeploy mints a *new* module rather than mutating the existing one.
327	`ContinuedAsNew` begins a new run and re-derives against whatever version that
328	new run binds to, which is correct rather than a gap.
329	
330	⇒ Implementations must read the authored list from **the run's own bound module
331	version**, never from the currently deployed package. The current-deploy reading
332	produces identical behaviour in every test — the two only diverge for a workflow
333	that was mid-hop when a new version landed, and then replay derives a different
334	queue sequence than history recorded. That is a long-lived-workflow replay break
335	that is invisible until the moment it matters, which is the class of defect this
336	engine exists to eliminate.
337	
338	## Implementation boundaries and gates
339	
340	L2 owns only classification and presentation: adapter recognition,
341	`HarnessError::PolicyRefused`, `ActivityErrorKind::PolicyRefused`, worker/server
342	mapping, regenerated bindings, and Gleam `policy_refused:` parsing/encoding.
343	
344	L3 owns only authored fallback and routing: AWL syntax/lowering, queue-chain
345	configuration, route recording, retry-loop consultation, recovery/replay, and
346	E2E coverage. L3 must consume L2's committed class rather than duplicating
347	recognition.
348	
349	Tests must establish:
350	
351	- structured norn data classifies as policy refusal while an ordinary generic
352	  JSON-RPC failure remains `Harness`;
353	- norn's admitted textual fallback is limited to the measured message field and
354	  phrase;
355	- ACP `StopReason::Refusal` classifies as policy refusal while max-token and
356	  max-turn stops do not;
357	- `is_deterministic()` is false, while worker conversion still emits the
358	  dedicated activity kind;
359	- worker bridge and Gleam preserve `policy_refused:`;
360	- a declared chain records refusal then hop and succeeds without a same-queue
361	  retry;
362	- no-chain behavior preserves the configured retry policy, attempts no hop, and
363	  terminates with policy-refused classification without asserting a particular
364	  count; and
365	- replay after each crash boundary described above chooses the same recorded
366	  queue.
367	
368	Any live-seat test is runtime-gated, logs its skip, and returns successfully
369	when the required environment is absent. No test is ignored and no blocking
370	sleep is sized to an expected run duration; asynchronous outcomes are polled
371	under a total deadline with timeout represented distinctly.

70	load-bearing-fact verdict (§2) and findings F-1..F-4 (§3) are all live and
71	authoritative, and F-1 in particular still blocks R1(c)'s "either is

74	Tom's ruling, 2026-08-22 09:50 his time, governs this flight: a provider
75	rejecting an act under its safety policy must not be a flight-killer.
76	"If there's an error like that, it can automatically retry with a
77	different one." Today the refusal arrives as `Retryable`, the engine
78	re-asks the SAME provider the SAME content four times (~25 min), and the
79	flight dies. Four flights died this way 08-20→08-21 (both #68
80	investigates, inv73-harness-flight2, beamr flight1). The cure is two
81	halves: (1) classify the refusal as its own class — never mislabelled as
82	a transient error, never burning the same-provider retry budget as if it
83	were one; (2) route around it: consult the declared chain FIRST (hop
84	first, retry second), any same-provider retry bounded by the act's
85	CONFIGURED budget.
86	
87	Seam provenance: exploration of tree `89ab967a` (branch regate/inv87r2)
88	— re-derive every line number on your tree; the SEAMS are the contract.
89	
90	## The defect chain, precisely (all five seams cited)
91	
92	1. norn adapter wraps the provider error verbatim:
93	   `crates/aion-integration-norn/src/session.rs:289` →
94	   `HarnessError::Harness` (`crates/aion-integrations/src/error.rs:78`).
95	   The provider's structured refusal (openai sse error event, code
96	   `cyber_policy`) is flattened to prose and never inspected.
97	2. `HarnessError::is_deterministic()` (`error.rs:223-233`) returns false
98	   for `Harness` ⇒ `harness_error_to_outcome()`
99	   (`crates/aion-worker/src/runtime/agent.rs:366-378`) marks it
100	   RETRYABLE.
101	3. The retry loop
102	   (`crates/aion/src/runtime/nif_activity_retry_dispatch.rs:247-330`)
103	   clones the request mutating ONLY `delivery.attempt` (:264-265) —
104	   per-attempt provider variation is foreclosed by design (negative test
105	   `crates/aion-integration-norn/src/harness.rs:639-645`).
106	4. `failure_stand_down()` (:183-203) wraps exhaustion:
107	   "exhausted: spent N of N attempts; last refusal: retryable:…".
108	5. The Gleam grammar (`gleam/aion_flow/src/aion/internal/
109	   activity_dispatch.gleam:134-160`) has no arm for `exhausted:` — it
110	   falls through to `ActivityEngineFailure`, so a content refusal
111	   presents to the operator as an ENGINE fault.
112	
113	## R1 — THE DESIGN ARTIFACT. Committed before implementation:
114	`docs/design/policy-refused-fallback.md` in-repo, deciding with rationale:
115	
116	- (a) **Detection seam**: where the provider's policy refusal is
117	  recognized. The template is the one existing text-inspection decorator
118	  `crates/aion-integration-norn/src/advice.rs` (`AdvisingHarness`,
119	  composition root `crates/aion-cli/src/harness/compose.rs:54-59`) — but
120	  today it only rewrites messages; RE-CLASSIFICATION is new capability.
121	  Prefer the provider's STRUCTURED code (`cyber_policy` in the sse error
122	  event) over substring matching wherever the adapter still holds the
123	  structured object; name where that object is last available. Cover the
124	  ACP adapter's equivalent surface
125	  (`crates/aion-integration-acp/src/outcome.rs:180-204`) or state with
126	  evidence why ACP cannot express a policy refusal.
127	- (b) **The new class**: `HarnessError::PolicyRefused` (enum at
128	  `error.rs:16-113`, `#[non_exhaustive]`). The exhaustive
129	  `is_deterministic()` match gets its arm decided ON PURPOSE (the
130	  crate's own doc :190-194 demands exactly this) — and per the
131	  correction above, the arm is ARGUED against Exhibits A and B, never
132	  assumed: a refusal is stochastic, so the arm's duty is
133	  stop-mislabelling-as-transient plus route-first semantics, not a
134	  determinism claim. Sweep the listed match
135	  sites: `agent.rs:244-248`, `:327-331` (catch-alls that would swallow
136	  it silently), `advice.rs:138-155`, and the stale-able doc at
137	  `agent.rs:335-364`.
138	- (c) **The reason vocabulary**: new `policy_refused:` prefix beside
139	  `retryable:`/`terminal:`/`timeout:`
140	  (`crates/aion/src/runtime/nif_activity_retry.rs:31-96`, render sites
141	  `crates/aion-server/src/worker/bridge.rs:474-480` +
142	  `declared_body.rs:481-486`). DESIGN DECISION, argued in the artifact:
143	  whether `ActivityErrorKind` (`crates/aion-core/src/error.rs:8-14`)
144	  gains a variant — that is a wire + TS-codegen event
145	  (`generated_types.rs:222`) — or stays binary with `policy_refused:`
146	  carried in the prefixed reason. Either is acceptable; silent
147	  mislabelling is not.
148	- (d) **The fallback chain**: AWL-declarable, at the same altitude as
149	  `retry` (`ConfigLine`, `crates/aion-awl/src/ast/document.rs:540-541`;
150	  lowering twins `emitter/stmts.rs:154-180` +
151	  `mir/lower/activity.rs:274-285`) — e.g. `fallback <queue>[, <queue>…]`
152	  naming task queues, since a queue IS the provider-flavour selector
153	  (`PoolAddress`, `registry.rs:117-123`) and AWL has NO model field
154	  (model lives in the worker binary; that stays true — this flight does
155	  not invent one). Measured constraint (Vesper, 08-22, at the boxes):
156	  norn is structurally ChatGPT-only (`norn auth login` offers ChatGPT
157	  alone) — a provider change is NECESSARILY a queue/harness hop; the
158	  chain design must not assume any in-harness model rotation. Semantics to pin down in the artifact: a
159	  PolicyRefused outcome consults the chain and re-dispatches the act on
160	  the next queue; chain hops are their own budget (the chain's length),
161	  DISTINCT from the retry budget — a policy refusal never burns
162	  same-provider retry attempts (`failure_stand_down` :194 must not
163	  count it retry-eligible). Chain exhausted ⇒ the act fails as
164	  `policy_refused:` with every refusing queue named. No chain declared
165	  ⇒ a bounded same-provider retry REMAINS (measurement: refusals
166	  sometimes clear on retry — Exhibits A and B), the bound CONFIGURED by
167	  the act's own retry declaration, never minted here; on exhaustion the
168	  act fails `policy_refused:` with the attempts accounted.
169	- (e) **Replay determinism**: the re-dispatch must be recorded in
170	  history such that replay re-derives the same queue sequence
171	  (`resolve_task_queue` precedence + `start_time_task_queue` replay
172	  note, `crates/aion/src/runtime/nif_activity.rs:77-113` — the design
173	  says how the fallback hop composes with that).
174	
175	## R2 — IMPLEMENTATION, per the committed design only
176	
177	Both halves land together: classification (adapter → `PolicyRefused` —
178	its own class, never mislabelled transient) and routing (chain consulted
179	first, honored end-to-end; same-provider retry only under the act's
180	configured bound). The Gleam grammar gains its arms — `parse_error/1`,
181	`encode_error/1` (`activity_dispatch.gleam:134-195`),
182	`describe_activity_error/1` (`awl/error.gleam:160-175`), `mock.gleam:80-90`
183	— so `policy_refused:` presents as itself, never as "activity engine
184	failure". While there, do NOT widen scope to the pre-existing
185	`exhausted:`/`infrastructure:` fallthrough mislabelling — REPORT it as a
186	named finding (it deserves its own item), don't fix it silently.
187	
188	## R3 — GREEN, DEFINED PRECISELY
189	
190	1. Unit: a synthetic provider policy refusal (structured code) classifies
191	   `PolicyRefused`; an ordinary harness error still classifies `Harness`
192	   retryable — both directions tested.
193	2. E2E (env-gated per house rules if it needs live seats): an act whose
194	   worker refuses by policy re-dispatches to the declared fallback queue
195	   and COMPLETES there; history shows one refusal + one hop, zero
196	   same-queue retries; `failure_reason` empty (the run succeeded).
197	3. E2E negative: no chain declared ⇒ the act exhausts its CONFIGURED
198	   retry bound and fails `policy_refused:` — assert the CLASSIFICATION
199	   and that NO chain hop was attempted, with attempt accounting in the
200	   record; assert no particular attempt count (the invariant, not the
201	   enumeration).
202	4. The Gleam surface: a `policy_refused:` failure presents with that
203	   prefix, not "activity engine failure" (assertion on the projected
204	   `failure_reason`, `crates/aion-core/src/filter.rs:176-206` path).
205	5. Full workspace gates green, two-instrument protocol per venue config.
206	
207	## Process walls — binding
208	
209	- No lint suppressions in any spelling; no `#[ignore]` in any spelling;
210	  runtime env-gates only. No file over 500 lines. `thiserror` errors;
211	  never `.unwrap()`/`.expect()` in library code. Wire/TS changes, if the
212	  design chooses them, regenerate — never hand-edit — generated types.
213	- ⛔ Never one blocking sleep sized to expected duration; poll + total
214	  deadline + timeout-as-distinct-outcome.
215	- Report path per the workflow's injected wire contract; `git ls-tree`
216	  receipt before the leg declares done.
217	- Measured red = success outcome under the F6 wall: if the design pass
218	  concludes the fallback hop cannot be made replay-deterministic without
219	  restructuring beyond this scope, that conclusion with evidence is the
220	  deliverable — committed, reported, no heroics.
221	
222	## The sentence to hold on to
223	
224	A policy refusal is a routing fact before it is a retry candidate.
225	**Classify it once, and route around the wall before grinding against
226	it.**

1	//! The harness-neutral error taxonomy for the integration seam.
2	//!
3	//! [`HarnessError`] is the single error type every [`crate::AgentHarness`] /
4	//! [`crate::AgentSession`] method returns. It is **harness-neutral**: no variant names a
5	//! concrete harness, and only the transport/protocol variants reference the notion of a wire
6	//! at all (as generic descriptions, never a specific protocol type). An adapter maps its own
7	//! failures onto these variants; callers above the adapter branch on the variant alone.
8	
9	/// How an adapter recognised a provider policy refusal.
10	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
11	pub enum PolicyRefusalDetection {
12	    /// A typed or structured discriminator identified the refusal.
13	    Structured,
14	    /// The adapter matched a documented, narrowly bounded provider message.
15	    Textual,
16	}
17	
18	/// The neutral error taxonomy for the harness-integration seam.
19	///
20	/// Every arm is harness-neutral. [`Self::CapabilityNotSupported`] is the first-class outcome an
21	/// observability-only harness returns from [`crate::AgentSession::intervene`] for any command —
22	/// it is a legitimate, gated rejection, not an internal failure.
23	#[derive(thiserror::Error, Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
24	#[non_exhaustive]
25	pub enum HarnessError {
26	    /// The requested intervention primitive is not in the harness's advertised capability set.
27	    ///
28	    /// This is the first-class rejection an observability-only harness (empty capability set)
29	    /// returns for *every* command, and the rejection any harness returns for a primitive it did
30	    /// not advertise. It is a normal, expected outcome of capability gating — not a fault.
31	    #[error("capability not supported: {primitive}")]
32	    CapabilityNotSupported {
33	        /// A neutral label naming the unsupported primitive (e.g. `"pause_resume"`).
34	        primitive: String,
35	    },
36	    /// The command targets a stale or unknown activity attempt and is a no-op.
37	    ///
38	    /// A command addressed to a superseded attempt (a later attempt is now live) or to a session
39	    /// that has already reached its terminal result is dropped without effect.
40	    #[error("stale target: {detail}")]
41	    StaleTarget {
42	        /// Human-readable detail describing why the target is stale.
43	        detail: String,
44	    },
45	    /// The spawn target is held by a live sibling process, so no run was started.
46	    ///
47	    /// A TRANSIENT refusal, and its own variant precisely because it must NOT classify like
48	    /// [`Self::Configuration`]: nothing anybody WROTE is wrong. The declared working tree is
49	    /// occupied by a live process — a surviving attempt from before a server death, or the
50	    /// previous workflow's agent still winding down in a sequentially reused tree — and the
51	    /// occupancy ends the moment the holder exits or dies, at which point the stale-marker
52	    /// cleanup admits the next claimant. The guard's refusal stays absolute while the holder
53	    /// lives; only its CLASSIFICATION is retryable. Field case: issue #33 — server-death
54	    /// recovery re-dispatched builder legs whose original processes had survived, and the
55	    /// terminal classification killed a two-hour fleet run over a condition that clears by
56	    /// itself. The worker maps this variant to a RETRYABLE activity failure; how long to keep
57	    /// waiting belongs to the retry policy.
58	    #[error("spawn target occupied: {detail}")]
59	    Occupied {
60	        /// Human-readable detail naming the live holder (pid, workflow, activity).
61	        detail: String,
62	    },
63	    /// The underlying transport failed (spawn/connect failure, broken pipe, EOF, I/O error).
64	    ///
65	    /// Neutral: it describes *that* the transport failed and carries the detail, never *which*
66	    /// transport. An adapter maps its own I/O failures here.
67	    #[error("transport error: {detail}")]
68	    Transport {
69	        /// Human-readable description of the transport failure.
70	        detail: String,
71	    },
72	    /// A message was received that violates the wire protocol contract.
73	    ///
74	    /// Malformed framing, an undecodable envelope, a response that correlates to no outstanding
75	    /// request, or a terminal result delivered on the wrong message kind. This signals a bug in
76	    /// the peer or the adapter, distinct from an ordinary transport outage.
77	    #[error("protocol error: {detail}")]
78	    Protocol {
79	        /// Human-readable description of the protocol violation.
80	        detail: String,
81	    },
82	    /// The harness reported an application-level failure while running the agent.
83	    ///
84	    /// The agent ran but ended in failure (a non-success exit, an error result, a rejected run).
85	    /// Distinct from [`Self::Transport`] (the channel broke) and [`Self::Protocol`] (a malformed
86	    /// message): here the channel and framing were sound and the harness *reported* failure.
87	    #[error("harness reported failure: {detail}")]
88	    Harness {
89	        /// Human-readable description of the reported failure.
90	        detail: String,
91	    },
92	    /// The provider declined to execute the run under its safety policy.
93	    ///
94	    /// This is stochastic: the same content has succeeded on a later attempt, so
95	    /// [`Self::is_deterministic`] returns `false`. It remains distinct from
96	    /// [`Self::Harness`] because callers route on this class before considering an
97	    /// ordinary same-provider retry.
98	    #[error("provider policy refused the run: {detail}")]
99	    PolicyRefused {
100	        /// Human-readable adapter-owned detail preserving the provider's refusal.
101	        detail: String,
102	        /// Whether recognition used a structured discriminator or admitted prose.
103	        detection: PolicyRefusalDetection,
104	    },
105	    /// The harness cannot be launched as CONFIGURED, so no run was started.
106	    ///
107	    /// A DETERMINISTIC refusal, and its own variant for the same reason
108	    /// [`Self::Contract`] is: the channel never opened, so [`Self::Transport`] is wrong
109	    /// and would tell an operator a story about a flaky pipe; no frame was exchanged, so
110	    /// [`Self::Protocol`] is wrong; and nothing ran, so [`Self::Harness`] is wrong. What
111	    /// is wrong is a value somebody WROTE — an environment pass-through entry that is a
112	    /// `KEY=VALUE` pair instead of a name, a declaration that omits the variable the
113	    /// program is looked up on. The next attempt reads the same document and meets the
114	    /// same wall, so retrying spends a worker's attempt budget to learn nothing. The
115	    /// worker maps this variant to a TERMINAL activity failure.
116	    #[error("harness configuration refusal: {detail}")]
117	    Configuration {
118	        /// Human-readable description naming the setting and what is wrong with it.
119	        detail: String,
120	    },
121	    /// The run completed, but its native outcome cannot satisfy the canonical
122	    /// agent-outcome contract
123	    /// (`AgentOutcome { text, final_message, stop_reason, session_id }`).
124	    ///
125	    /// A DETERMINISTIC refusal, and that is the whole reason it is its own variant: the channel
126	    /// was sound ([`Self::Transport`] is wrong), the frames were well-formed ([`Self::Protocol`]
127	    /// is wrong — and a protocol fault CAN be a transient peer flake, which this never is), and
128	    /// the run did not fail ([`Self::Harness`] is wrong). The run's *configuration* produces an
129	    /// outcome the seam excludes — e.g. a structured output where the contract's `text` demands a
130	    /// String — so re-running it re-spends a whole agent run to hit the same wall. The worker
131	    /// maps this variant to a TERMINAL activity failure; every other variant stays retryable.
132	    #[error("agent-outcome contract refusal: {detail}")]
133	    Contract {
134	        /// Human-readable description naming the contract and what was found.
135	        detail: String,
136	    },
137	}
